title: kt-null-graph-controls: code and run files for "When does a concept graph help a knowledge tracer? Entry-point null-graph controls and decision stability for KC-level learner models"
description:
Code, run files and analysis scripts for the manuscript "When does a concept graph help a knowledge tracer? Entry-point null-graph controls and decision stability for KC-level learner models" (H. B. Truong, under revision for User Modeling and User-Adapted Interaction).

The study fixes KC-level tracers and measures a concept graph against an empty-graph control that keeps every other parameter, a ladder of null graphs, fixed random codes and capacity controls on ten public corpora, at five entry points (embedding refinement, attention bias, state channel, the training loss of PDKT and the propagation of GKT), with a replication on two held-out corpora under a pre-specified plan. Every run file, analysis output and script behind the tables and figures of the manuscript and its Online Resources is under kt/; unit tests in tests/.

Version 5.0.0 adds the runs and analyses of the UMUAI revision (kt/src/r19_*.py, kt/src/prep_r19.py, kt/runs_r19, kt/results_r19): 142 new training runs and 11 reruns that reproduce archived runs to the last digit on the rebuilt corpora. New run sets: a support graph built from all training learners given to a tracer trained on 10% of them (transfer of structure), the null-graph ladder inside PDKT, three training seeds per subsample, 5% probes with candidate scores for the decision analysis, a 500-interaction cap on two larger corpora, and XES3G5M without multi-KC questions. New analyses: first-attempt references (KC rate, PFA-style model) with pooled, per-learner and within-KC AUC; graph quality by training size; four interval methods and a seed-based smallest effect of interest; Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment over the exploratory terms; next-KC decisions under a Rasch and a learning simulator with a stabilized target rule (tolerance band and curriculum tie-break). Earlier content (releases 2.0.0 to 4.1.0) is unchanged.
